claim_2.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees across multiple influenza seasons showed that interferon and dendritic-cell blood transcriptional modules on days 1 and 3 after vaccination were positively associated with day 28 HAI responses, whereas T-cell modules at these time points were negatively associated and ASC and cell-cycle modules were robustly enriched on day 7 compared to lower-response signatures.

claim_3.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of baseline PBMCs from combined influenza vaccine studies showed that pre-vaccination B-cell- and T-cell-related modules were positively correlated with increased day 28 antibody responses, whereas monocyte-related modules were negatively correlated compared to lower responders.

claim_4.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly vaccinees in the 2010 and 2011 seasons showed that NK-cell-related modules increased with age on days 3 and 7 after vaccination, several monocyte modules increased with age on day 7, and many B-cell modules decreased with age compared to younger subjects.

claim_5.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 vaccinees across days 0–14 after vaccination showed that elderly subjects had higher total NK-cell proportions than young subjects at baseline and all measured time points, with vaccination increasing NK-cell percentages in the elderly but reducing them on day 1 in the young.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Our analysis showed that proportions of total NK cells in elderly subjects were higher than those of young subjects at baseline as well as at all the time points studied (days 0–14).

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Of note, vaccination induced an increase in the percentage of NK cells in the elderly subjects; in contrast, in the young there was a reduction in the percentage of NK cells on day 1 after vaccination ( Figure 5A ).

claim_6.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 vaccinees showed that elderly subjects had a higher baseline frequency of CD56dim CD16++ NK cells and a lower frequency of CD56++ NK cells than young subjects, with CD56dim CD16++ cells increasing significantly in the elderly on day 1 after vaccination and CD56++ cells increasing in the young on day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: We observed a higher frequency of CD56 dim CD16 ++ cells coincident with a lower frequency of CD56 ++ cells in the elderly at baseline, consistent with previous studies ( Figure 5C ; Solana et al., 2014 ).

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: The distribution of these subpopulations was relatively stable during the response, with CD56 dim CD16 ++ cells showing a small but significant increase in the elderly on day 1 after vaccination and CD56 ++ cells increasing in the young on day 7.

claim_7.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 vaccinees showed that NK-cell activation measured by CD69 increased after vaccination in all three NK subsets in elderly subjects with highest expression on day 3, whereas young subjects showed CD69 activation only in the CD56dim CD16++ subset on day 1 and at a lower level than in the elderly.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Elderly subjects showed increasing activation after vaccination in all three subsets, with highest expression on day 3.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: In contrast, the young exhibited activation of the CD56 dim CD16 ++ subset as measured by CD69 expression only on day 1 and at a lower level than in the elderly.

claim_8.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 vaccinees showed that elderly subjects had higher monocyte proportions than young subjects at baseline and throughout the study, both groups showed substantial increases in total monocyte percentages on day 1 after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0), and elderly subjects had increased CCR5 but lower CD86 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to young subjects.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: In addition to NK cells, we also observed higher proportions of monocytes among the elderly at baseline and during the entire duration of the study compared to young subjects ( Figure S6A ).

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: In both groups, the percentage of total monocytes in PBMCs increased substantially on day 1 after vaccination, then returned to or below baseline levels.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Elderly subjects showed increased CCR5 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to the young, whereas young subjects had higher CD86 expression in these subsets.

claim_9.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of plasma from 62 vaccinees followed through day 180 showed that antibody responses peaked at day 28 after vaccination and declined significantly by day 180, with temporary responders meeting seroconversion criteria at day 28 but not day 180 and persistent responders meeting criteria at both time points.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: The antibody responses peaked at day 28 (D28), with a significant decline in most subjects by D180 ( Figure 6A ).

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: By applying the same criteria for seroconversion used for the D28 high- versus low-responder classification to the D180 antibody responses, we saw that just over half of D28 high responders maintained their responder status on day 180 (“persistent” responders), whereas the remainder no longer met the criteria for seroconversion on day 180 (“temporary” responders).

claim_10.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees with day 180 follow-up showed that plasmablast module BTM S3 was positively associated with the day 180 antibody response because of its relationship to day 28 titers, but it was not associated with the adjusted day 180/day 28 residual, while modules related to cell movement and adhesion were enriched in persistent responders and several T-cell-related modules at day 7 were negatively associated with persistence compared to waning responders.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: As expected, correlation analysis of plasmablast module BTM S3 shows a positive association with the D180 antibody response due to the effect of D28 antibody responses, generated through plasmablast expansion ( Figure 6C ).

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: However, when we performed correlation between the plasmablast module activity and the D180/D28 residual, we no longer saw an association with the plasmablast expression ( Figure 6D ).

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: Among the BTMs most enriched in subjects with a persistent response on both days 3 and 7 were several modules associated with cell movement and adhesion, such as BTM 51 ( Figure 6E ).

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: In addition, the day 7 expression of a number of T-cell-related modules was negatively associated with the D180/D28 residual, indicating that increased T cell responses might potentially result in more transient antibody responses ( Figure 6F ).

claim_11.claim: miRNA expression profiling analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 vaccinees on days 1, 3, and 7 after vaccination showed that elderly subjects had predominantly upregulated miRNAs after vaccination, especially on days 1 and 7, whereas young subjects showed predominantly downregulated miRNAs, and the elderly had more miRNAs negatively correlated with day 28 HAI responses than the young.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: Whereas a majority of the differentially expressed miRNA in the elderly were upregulated after vaccination, particularly on days 1 and 7, the young exhibited predominantly downregulation of miRNA.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: We again saw differences between the young and elderly subjects, with the elderly having a larger number of miRNA negatively correlating with the antibody response when compared with the young.

claim_12.claim: miRNA expression profiling analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 vaccinees showed that day 1 miRNA expression correlated with blood transcriptional modules, and integration with TargetScan identified a putative regulatory network for the day 1 antiviral interferon module M75 in which miR-424 was predicted to target OAS3 and CXCL10.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: We then performed correlation analysis between all miRNA-BTM pairs, revealing groups of modules that appear to be regulated together by several miRNA ( Figure 7D ) on day 1 after vaccination.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: Of particular interest was the regulation of module M75-antiviral interferon signature ( Figure 7E ) on day 1 after vaccination, because the interferon pathway plays a key role during the innate immune response.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: This miRNA-mRNA network suggests potential novel regulators of the interferon response after vaccination, such as miR-424. This miRNA was predicted to target OAS3, a 2′–5′-oligoadenylate synthase involved in viral RNA degradation ( Samuel, 2001 ), as well as CXCL10, an important chemokine induced by IFN-γ that serves as a chemoattractant for lymphocytes ( Dufour et al., 2002 ).
